description: Evidence-based spatial design framework connecting human biology and psychology to nature, daylight, circadian rhythms, thermal variations, and living ecological systems.
schools_note: Grounds design decisions in empirical environmental psychology, cognitive neuroscience, and building physics rather than spiritual dogma.

value.notes: Occupants must have an unobstructed sightline to living plants, courtyard greenery, or open sky within 6.0 meters.

rules.rationale: Visual connection to living natural systems reduces blood pressure, cortisol levels, and mental fatigue within 3 to 5 minutes.
rules.source: Browning, W.D. et al., '14 Patterns of Biophilic Design' (Terrapin Bright Green, 2014), Pattern 1, pp. 22-25

value.notes: Minimum Daylight Factor >= 2.0% in primary habitable rooms.

rules.rationale: Exposure to dynamic morning daylight spectrum suppresses melatonin, stabilizes human circadian rhythms, and improves sleep quality.
rules.source: WELL Building Standard v2, Feature L01 (Light Exposure) & Terrapin Pattern 6, pp. 38-41

value.notes: Air velocity variability between 0.3 m/s and 0.8 m/s.

rules.rationale: Non-rhythmic sensory stimuli and natural thermal variations keep human alertness high and reduce Sick Building Syndrome (SBS).
rules.source: Terrapin Bright Green Pattern 3 (Thermal & Airflow Variability), pp. 30-33 & NBC 2016 Part 8

rules.rationale: Gentle, non-rhythmic acoustic murmur of trickling water masks harsh urban traffic noise and induces autonomic parasympathetic relaxation.
rules.source: Terrapin Bright Green Pattern 5 (Presence of Water), pp. 34-37 & Ulrich, R.S. Psycho-evolutionary Theory (1991)

rules.rationale: Haptic and visual resonance with natural grain, geological striations, and patinating surfaces reduces sympathetic stress arousal.
rules.source: Kellert, S.R. & Calabrese, E.F., 'The Practice of Biophilic Design' (2015), Ch. 2

value.notes: Enclosed back and overhead plane while overlooking open courtyard or garden.

rules.rationale: Prospect & Refuge: Evolutionary preference for sheltered, protected resting spots (refuge) providing a broad view of the surrounding terrain (prospect).
rules.source: Appleton, Jay. 'The Experience of Landscape' (1975) & Terrapin Patterns 11 & 12, pp. 54-61

value.notes: Shaded vegetation and open sky inducing convective chimney cooling.

rules.rationale: Central courtyard lowers peak interior summer ambient temperature by 3°C to 5°C through evapotranspiration and nighttime radiative cooling.
rules.source: Givoni, B., 'Man, Climate and Architecture' & CEPT University Passive Solar Housing Compendium

value.notes: Target: 1 medium-sized plant per 9 square meters of floor area.

rules.rationale: Phytoremediation: Plant-soil root microbiomes absorb airborne VOCs (benzene, formaldehyde, trichloroethylene) and replenish indoor oxygen levels.
rules.source: Wolverton, B.C., NASA Clean Air Study (1989) & Terrapin Pattern 2, pp. 26-29
